tools.name: addMyAssignmentNote
tools.description: POST /api/v1/me/assignments/{id}/notes. Add a note to an assignment. APPENDS to whatever notes are already there rather than replacing them: the endpoint is called add-a-note, and a write that silently overwrote would lose the student own writing the first time it was used. Replace outright with PATCH /me/assignments/{id} instead.

tools.name: createMyAssignment
tools.description: POST /api/v1/me/assignments. Add an assignment. Needs a title. A course_id is checked against your own courses first, so an assignment cannot be filed against a stranger course. An omitted or null due_at means the date is unknown — it is never invented.

tools.name: createMyCourse
tools.description: POST /api/v1/me/courses. Create a course by hand. At least a code or a name. Credits default to 3 only when nothing is given — a wrong credit count silently breaks the full-time check, the cost estimate and the degree audit at once, so it is never inferred from anything else.

tools.name: createMyCourseFromOutline
tools.description: POST /api/v1/me/courses/from-outline. Create a course by uploading a syllabus PDF. Send the PDF as the raw request body with Content-Type application/pdf. Runs the SAME extractor as the website upload — literally the same function — so an outline cannot parse one way in the browser and another way here. Creates the course and its assessments, and returns both plus the weight total. Dates the outline does not give come back null and are never guessed. Max 4 MB.

tools.name: deleteMyAssignment
tools.description: DELETE /api/v1/me/assignments/{id}. Remove an assignment. Soft delete. The row is marked deleted and disappears from every view, including the GPA, but is not destroyed — a script deleting the wrong row is a likelier accident than a person doing it, and one of the two should be recoverable.

tools.name: deleteMyCourse
tools.description: DELETE /api/v1/me/courses/{id}. Archive a course, or really delete it. Archives by default: a course with grades in it is a record, and clearing a term to tidy a list is the sort of thing somebody regrets. hard=true really removes it, and takes its assignments with it — they do not cascade, so a plain delete would leave rows still counting toward a GPA for a course that no longer exists.

hard.description: true deletes instead of archiving. There is no undo.

tools.name: getMyAssignment
tools.description: GET /api/v1/me/assignments/{id}. One assignment, in full. Everything on it, including the notes and the grade.

tools.name: getMyCalendar
tools.description: GET /api/v1/me/calendar. Everything dated, grouped by day. Assignments and personal or Moodle tasks in a date range, bucketed on the LOCAL date the way the calendar screen buckets them — slicing an ISO string would report a 23:59 deadline as the next day in UTC. An assignment with no date is not here, because we do not know when it is. Defaults to the last week and the next sixty days.

from.description: Start of the range. Defaults to seven days ago.

to.description: End of the range. Defaults to sixty days ahead.

tools.name: getMyCourse
tools.description: GET /api/v1/me/courses/{id}. One course, with its assignments. The course plus every assignment on it, and a summary: how many there are, how many are graded, and what the weights add up to. A total that is not 100 is worth looking at.

tools.name: getSupportKbArticle
tools.description: GET /api/v1/support/kb/{id}. One knowledge base article, in full. The whole body. Fetch the article you intend to quote: the list and the search return snippets only, so what you quoted is the article you asked for.

id.description: The article id, as returned by the list or the search.

tools.name: getSupportThread
tools.description: GET /api/v1/support/threads/{id}. One thread, with its messages. A diagnostic returns a single message authored by `user` carrying the notes and the payload, so a client needs one code path rather than two. `can_reply` says whether this thread will accept a reply right now.

id.description: A composite thread id, e.g. t:9c1e… or d:4b77….

tools.name: listSupportThreads
tools.description: GET /api/v1/support/threads. Support threads, newest activity first. Two kinds of thread. A `ticket` is anything a customer wrote and is a conversation; a `diagnostic` is an automated report and cannot be replied to. Ids are composite and stable: `t:<uuid>` and `d:<uuid>`. `since` matches threads created OR updated at/after the timestamp, so an old thread with a new customer message is returned.

type.description: Only conversations, or only automated reports.

status.description: Only threads currently in this state.

since.description: ISO-8601. Matches creation OR last activity.

needs_human.description: Only threads flagged for a person, or only those not flagged. Omit for either. A thread held for crisis or money reads as true whether or not anyone set it.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous page. Page with this rather than an offset: threads reorder as they are answered, so an offset scan silently skips whatever moved up while you were reading. A null next_cursor means there is no more.

tools.name: myAssignments
tools.description: GET /api/v1/me/assignments. Your deadlines. Every assessment on your account, earliest first. `upcoming=true` means dated and not yet past — an UNDATED item is not upcoming, because we do not know that it is.

course_id.description: Only assessments belonging to this course.

status.description: Only assessments currently in this state.

upcoming.description: Only assessments that are dated and not yet past. An undated one is excluded, because we do not know that it is upcoming.

q.description: Keyword search over the title AND the description, so a phrase that is in the blurb rather than the name still finds it.

due_before.description: ISO-8601, or the word now. Undated assignments are excluded.

due_after.description: ISO-8601, or the word now. Undated assignments are excluded.

tools.name: myCourses
tools.description: GET /api/v1/me/courses. Your courses. The classes on your account for the current term, or the finished ones with `archived=true`. Each carries its code, title, term, credits, section and instructor.

archived.description: Return finished courses instead of current ones.

tools.name: myGpa
tools.description: GET /api/v1/me/gpa. Your standing, per course and overall. Each course percentage is a weighted average over the weight graded SO FAR, not out of 100, and the denominator is returned as `graded_weight` so nobody has to guess which of the two it is. A course with nothing graded reports null, never zero.

tools.name: patchSupportThread
tools.description: PATCH /api/v1/support/threads/{id}. Change a thread state. Either field, or both. Use it to ESCALATE: set needs_human true and leave the thread for a person. Setting `ai_handling` CLEARS `needs_human` — the hand-back gesture, one call so there is no window where the assistant owns a thread still flagged for a person. `resolved` is REFUSED for this token (409 `resolve_is_human_only`): deciding a customer problem is over is a judgement with a person name on it. A diagnostic refuses handling changes with 409.

tools.name: replyToSupportThread
tools.description: POST /api/v1/support/threads/{id}/replies. Reply to a customer. Stored with author `ai`. Replying to an `open` thread moves it to `ai_handling`. WHETHER A REPLY IS ALLOWED IS DECIDED IN THE DATABASE, not here, so no caller can route around it. A refusal is 409 with a machine-readable `reason`: `crisis_hold` (the customer mentioned self-harm — never answered automatically; follow the crisis protocol and leave it for a person), `money_hold` (a refund, discount or delivery date — those are promises a person makes), `human_takeover`, `resolved`, `needs_human`, or `diagnostic_not_repliable`. Every accepted reply is written to the admin audit log with its exact wording.

id.description: A composite thread id. Diagnostics cannot be replied to.

body.description: The reply. Never write an assistant label into it — the UI renders that from the author field.

tools.name: searchSupportKb
tools.description: GET /api/v1/support/kb. List every knowledge base article. Id, title, url and summary for every article — no bodies, because forty articles of prose is most of a context window spent on pages that will not be used. Generated from the published documentation and the legal documents, so they cannot drift from what a person would be told to read. Answer ONLY from these.

q.description: Keywords. Omit to list every article.

tools.name: searchSupportKbArticles
tools.description: GET /api/v1/support/kb/search. Search the knowledge base. Scored across title, id, summary and body, best first, with a snippet around the match so relevance can be judged without fetching each one. A body hit counts once per article, so a long page mentioning a word in passing does not outrank the page about it. NOTHING MATCHING IS AN ANSWER: escalate rather than replying from memory.

tools.name: setMyAssignmentGrade
tools.description: PATCH /api/v1/me/assignments/{id}/grade. Set or clear a grade. Either a percentage or a raw score. The same thing PATCH /me/assignments/{id} does with a grade field, as its own verb.

tools.name: updateMyAssignment
tools.description: PATCH /api/v1/me/assignments/{id}. Tick something off, or record a grade. Changes status, grade or notes — the same narrow set the app itself allows. Not weights, dates or provenance: a weight edited by a script is a grade computed from a number nobody checked, and provenance is a claim about where a date came from that a token cannot honestly make. Returns the row as it now stands.

id.description: The assessment to change, as returned by /api/v1/me/assignments.

grade.description: Either {percent} or {earned,total}. null clears the grade.

tools.name: updateMyCourse
tools.description: PATCH /api/v1/me/courses/{id}. Update a course. Any of code, name, term, credits, colour, section, instructor, location, meeting_times, office_hours, syllabus_url, grading_scale, enrollment or archived. Fields are named explicitly rather than passed through, so nothing can set user_id and hand the course to somebody else.
